criteria.criterion: what the tables are, and the five aggregates kept out of them by name
criteria.detail: 212,805 class-cells on the 20 NACE sections, 36,288 on the five aggregates that are sums of them (M-N, MARKT, NMARKT, TOT, TOT_IND) and are excluded by name rather than silently. 621 country-year tables with three or more industries, rows min 9 median 19 max 20; 527 industry-year tables with three or more countries, rows min 8 median 33 max 37. Columns are the 18 classes in every table.
criteria.name: B106-1

criteria.criterion: a separable field reads zero and a field with no structure reads its own degrees of freedom
criteria.detail: separable in, zero out: worst interaction share 6.84e-32 over 15 draws. No structure in, the degrees of freedom out: J=4 0.7230 vs (J-1)(K-1)/(JK-1) = 0.7183 (z 0.14), J=8 0.8088 vs (J-1)(K-1)/(JK-1) = 0.8322 (z 1.19), J=19 0.9129 vs (J-1)(K-1)/(JK-1) = 0.8974 (z 1.50); worst z 1.50 against four standard errors of the exact Beta over 5 draws
criteria.name: B106-2

criteria.criterion: how much of the field no scalar on positions plus a class ladder can produce
criteria.detail: countries_within_industry_year: 527 tables, interaction share median 0.4353 against a no-structure 0.9174, ratio 0.502, below half of it in 262; industries_within_country_year: 621 tables, interaction share median 0.4027 against a no-structure 0.8974, ratio 0.450, below half of it in 366
criteria.name: B106-3

criteria.criterion: whether what is left over repeats next year, which survey noise does not
criteria.detail: countries_within_industry_year: 197,622 adjacent-year pairs, correlation +0.9545, which is 424 standard errors from the rival's zero; ten years apart +0.6684 over 85,050; with the position pairing broken and every marginal kept, +0.1537 over 186,534; industries_within_country_year: 197,622 adjacent-year pairs, correlation +0.9544, which is 424 standard errors from the rival's zero; ten years apart +0.6790 over 85,050; with the position pairing broken and every marginal kept, +0.0510 over 168,354. Survey noise does not repeat, so the rival's reading is a point at zero. The decade-apart figure answers a compiler that interpolates between survey years, and the broken pairing answers the statistic itself.

grid_note.ours: the interaction is the square, two positions by two classes, and it is a standing feature of who is being paid where, so it repeats
grid_note.rival: it is zero, so what is measured is noise and does not repeat

criteria.name: B106-4
criteria.rival_entailment: sampling error in one year is independent of sampling error in the next, so under that premise the interaction measured at a position and class in year t has zero correlation with the same position and class in year t+1. The prediction is a point at zero, with a standard error of one over the root of the pair count.
criteria.rival_premise: the price a class is paid at a position is a scalar on the position times a factor for the class, so in logs the field is additively separable and the interaction is identically zero; anything observed in it is sampling error in the survey the shares come from

criteria.criterion: whether the leftover shrinks where the class is large, which is what sampling noise does
criteria.detail: interaction residual by the class's own employment share, ten deciles from the smallest classes to the largest: d1 0.6894, d2 0.3987, d3 0.3419, d4 0.3177, d5 0.2845, d6 0.2666, d7 0.2505, d8 0.2558, d9 0.2496, d10 0.2265. The thinnest decile reads 0.6894 and the thickest 0.2265, a fall of 3.04 times across a span of at least 22 times in employment share. Sampling error would fall as one over the root of the count, which over that span is about 5 times, so the profile is far flatter than noise and it stops falling after the fifth decile: d5 to d10 move only from 0.2845 to 0.2265.
criteria.name: B106-5
